text:
Sam G: Customer ACME-Prod reports ~40 qps spike at 08:01 UTC, got sustained 429s and 1.2s median latency. Looks like dedicated pool didn't scale quickly.
Jess P: Triage started. Customer org id: org-acme-77. Can you attach request ids and any relevant logs?
autoscale-bot: detected scale_event
autoscale-bot: event=scale_attempt reason=surge_probe current_replicas=2 desired_replicas=12 holdoff_ms=45000 step_limit=2 last_scale_ts=2123456600
Rahul M: From runtime logs: scaler applied step_limit=2 + cooldown=60s -> for 40qps that's too slow, effectively a stepbeat backoff.
Marie L: Can you share the deployment policy? paste YAML or a small snippet.
Sam G: here's the config snippet the customer is on:
```
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 50
scale_step: 2
scale_cooldown_seconds: 60
probe_threshold_qps: 10
```
Jess P: Repro steps I used (on customer creds):
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD-ACME-TEST" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}' --rate 40 -c 10
(reproduces 429s within 30s)
Rahul M: Quick analysis: step-based limiter + cooldown causes linear climb 2->4->6... so ~25-30s per step -> ~90s to reach 12. For burst traffic we need a fast-path to allow larger initial step or a prewarm probe.
Marie L: Short-term mitigation: override customer's scale_step to 8 and reduce cooldown to 20s for their dedicated pool, then monitor. Ops, can we patch that config for org-acme-77?
Ops Bot: @Rahul M @Jess P submitted infra ticket INF-5432 to adjust scale policy for org-acme-77. will apply in staging then prod. ETA 20m. :clock1:
Sam G: Noted. Also adding customer success (cc @Lina C) for a heads-up and possible credits.
Jess P: I'll keep the customer updated. collecting request ids and sample logs now. :eyes:
